name: Dogs Trust (rabies control)
beneficiaries_note: Our build: WVS and Mission Rabies' dog vaccination by 2025 doses: India over half and Cambodia 221,391 (Mission Rabies' 2025 review), Laos 21,500; the rest over Malawi and the grant countries by grant size (a judgment).
summary: Dogs Trust's sister charity Worldwide Veterinary Service and its Mission Rabies project vaccinated 2.2 million dogs against rabies in 2025, with Dogs Trust grants to rabies programmes in Malawi, Cambodia, Guinea and Bangladesh; this model takes about a fifth of Dogs Trust's international spending ($6.9m, a judgment) for that work. Human deaths averted per dose come from Mission Rabies' own programme in Goa, India, where 426,000 doses from 2013 to 2019 averted an estimated 80 deaths and human rabies fell to zero: far more per dollar than Dogs Trust's dog-welfare work. The biggest uncertainties are whether WVS's other campaigns protect people as Goa's sustained one did (rabies deaths per dog where they were given, and how well coverage is kept up), the share of international spending that goes on rabies, and the missing-data discount, since the effect was measured only in Goa.

source.title: charityevals' estimate: Dogs Trust's rabies control through Worldwide Veterinary Service (2025)

resources.title: Gibson et al. 2022, Elimination of human rabies in Goa, India through an integrated One Health approach, Nature Communications 13:2788

sections.title: Cost
sections.explainer: What the modelled program cost in the year the outcomes below are counted for, including its share of overhead. From audited financial statements or the annual report.

sections.title: Reach
sections.explainer: How many people, animals or meals the spending reached in the same year, as the charity reports it.

sections.title: Effect per unit
sections.explainer: What the intervention does for each unit reached, from the best available studies, before any adjustment.

sections.title: Adjustments
sections.explainer: Discounts for weaker evidence, what would have happened anyway, credit shared with others, and delivery falling short. All multiply the outcome.

sections.title: Other outcomes, in this model's unit
sections.explainer: charityevals' standard step for outcomes in more than one unit (docs/normalization.md 2.6): each outcome is counted in its own unit (units of value for income and deaths, WELLBYs for life satisfaction, tonnes of CO₂e, chicken pain days) and put into this model's unit by its unit's conversion over this unit's, which the headline's conversion cancels. So each moves only with its own sliders, exactly as in a model of its own unit. The rows are fixed; don't edit them.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.explainer: The outcome in the family's shared unit, per dollar.

sections.title: Your dollar's share
sections.explainer: Staff who earn less than they could elsewhere pay part of the cost in kind. With credit by share of resources, your dollar is credited with its share of the full cost only.

rows.label: Human rabies deaths averted in Goa, 2013-2019

source.title: Gibson et al. 2022, Elimination of human rabies in Goa, India through an integrated One Health approach, Nature Communications 13:2788

rows.explainer: The paper's decision-tree estimate from bite-patient data against no programme; the range is ours (the paper's own interval is not given in the text read): 50 to 110.

rows.label: Dog-years of the population covered per dose (Goa: dogs × years ÷ doses)
rows.explainer: Each dose in Goa stood for 2.3 dog-years of the whole population at the coverage reached (about 70%): vaccinated dogs protect unvaccinated ones by stopping transmission.

rows.label: Human rabies deaths per dog per year (Goa, 2014)
rows.explainer: Deaths in Goa in 2014, early in the programme, over its dogs: 1.2 per 10,000 dogs a year. WVS's other places differ (external validity below).

rows.label: Share of the 2014 death rate averted over the programme
rows.explainer: 80 deaths averted against 17 a year for 7 years: two thirds. Human deaths fell to zero in 2018 and 2019.

rows.label: Other deaths averted per rabies death averted
rows.explainer: 0: the effect counted is deaths from rabies itself; there is no indirect mortality channel.

rows.label: Human deaths averted per dog vaccinated
Share of rabies deaths under age 5
rows.explainer: The shared age split of rabies deaths (facts/death_ages.json).

rows.label: Share aged 5-14 of deaths over 5
rows.explainer: From the shared age split.

rows.label: Share aged 15-49 of deaths over 15
rows.explainer: From the shared age split.

rows.label: Illness averted, as a share of the deaths' value
rows.explainer: Rabies is almost always fatal, so there is little illness to avert: bites by rabid dogs (wounds, fear) and courses of post-exposure prophylaxis. Our judgment 2%, 0 to 5%.

rows.label: Stillbirths averted per person reached (before adjustments)
rows.explainer: 0: rabies vaccination of dogs has no stillbirth channel.

rows.label: Later-life income gain per person reached, ln(consumption) per year
rows.explainer: 0: no later-life income gain is claimed for dog vaccination.

rows.label: Years until the income gain starts
rows.explainer: the site's one figure for the program (@givewell_shared.years_until_income_benefits_malaria, _smc, _iron or _deworming); for a program none fits, an estimate input from the study, with its source and range.

rows.label: Years the long-term income gain lasts
rows.explainer: The site's one figure for how long a long-term income gain lasts (GiveWell's working years, 40), read by every model that counts one (INV-13).

rows.label: Later-life income gain per person reached, present value
rows.explainer: Discounted at the shared rate, the wait included, so the result moves with it. Never type in a present value worked out elsewhere: rebuild it from its inputs.

rows.label: Resource sharing within households (multiplier on an earner's gain)
rows.explainer: The site's one figure (GiveWell's): an earner's income gain is shared with the household, so it counts this many times. Read by every model that values a long-term income gain (INV-13).

rows.label: Internal validity of the Goa estimate
rows.explainer: The deaths averted are modelled from bite-patient data against a no-vaccination counterfactual, not a controlled comparison; human deaths did fall to zero, so the direction is sure. 0.8, 0.6 to 0.95.

rows.label: Human rabies deaths per dog where WVS vaccinated in 2025, against Goa's

source.title: Mission Rabies, 2025: a year of impact
source.quote: over 1 million dogs were vaccinated in India alone

rows.explainer: Our judgment, weighted by 2025 doses (over half in India, Mission Rabies' 2025 review): per person, WHO's estimates for the dose-weighted countries are below Goa's 1.16 per 100,000, but per dog it depends on dog density, which is higher in many of them; the direction is open. 1, 0.4 to 2.5.

rows.label: How well 2025's campaigns keep coverage up, against Goa's
rows.explainer: Our judgment: Goa held about 70% coverage for years with surveillance; India's and Cambodia's drives are annual (Cambodia's third in 2025, p. 34) but coverage outside Goa is less often measured, and one-off drives lapse as dogs turn over. 0.6, 0.3 (thin, lapsing coverage) to 1 (as Goa).

rows.label: External validity: WVS's other campaigns against Goa's
rows.explainer: Goa's deaths averted per dose carried to WVS's 2025 doses: how much more often rabid dogs kill people where they were given, times how well the campaigns keep coverage up.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment (internal and external validity), a multiplier
rows.explainer: The product of its two parts.

rows.label: Share of the outcome that wouldn't have happened anyway
rows.explainer: Doses others would have given the same dogs anyway: owners' private vaccination and other NGOs; few free-roaming dogs are vaccinated otherwise. 0.85, 0.7 to 0.95. Government budgets' response is in leverage_funging_adj.

rows.label: In-country cost of a dog vaccination in Goa, 2018-19, US dollars (vaccine donated, not included)

source.title: Gibson et al. 2022, Elimination of human rabies in Goa, India through an integrated One Health approach, Nature Communications 13:2788
source.quote: mean cost per dog vaccinated of 3.45 USD

rows.explainer: Goa's programme cost per dog vaccinated from in-country spending; MSD donated all the vaccine, so it isn't in this figure. Low end the paper's global average (2.18 USD) for mass campaigns, high end harder catching.

rows.label: Value of the donated vaccine per dose, 2019 US dollars
rows.explainer: Our judgment of a canine rabies vaccine dose's price in bulk to campaigns (about half a dollar), 0.3 to 0.8.

rows.label: Full cost of a dog vaccination, 2025 US dollars
rows.explainer: In-country cost plus the vaccine, in 2025 prices (US CPI, Convention 8).

rows.label: This charity's share of the resources behind the outcome
rows.explainer: Dogs Trust's share of all resources behind each dose: what Dogs Trust paid per dose over the full cost of a dose (vaccine, vaccinators, catching, cold chain), capped at 1. Partners (donated vaccine, government vaccinators, volunteers) paid the rest. One number for cost and credit.

rows.label: Share of credit used
rows.explainer: The charity's share of the resources behind the outcome; it applies whichever way credit is shared.

rows.label: Delivery adjustment (fidelity, compliance, follow-through)
rows.explainer: 1: Goa's deaths averted per dose already include doses that didn't protect (cold chain, re-dosed dogs), so a delivery shortfall here would count twice (audit round 1).

rows.label: Leverage and funging
rows.explainer: Governments' budget response: they may vaccinate a little less where WVS does (funging) or more once it shows results; 0.95, 0.85 to 1.05.

rows.label: Years a donation waits before the charity spends it
rows.explainer: Dogs Trust spent about what it raised in 2025 (surplus £13.8m mostly from selling an office); a gift is spent within the year: 0.25, 0 to 1.

rows.label: Years from the charity's spending to the intervention reaching people
rows.explainer: Campaigns run through the year; a quarter of a year from spending to the dose, 0.1 to 0.5.

rows.label: Years from delivery to the middle of the protection
rows.explainer: The benefits come over the years of protection (a net's life, a season's doses), so they are discounted from its middle; 0 for a one-off effect such as a vaccine dose's.

rows.label: Discount for the wait until the benefits come
rows.explainer: Every wait is discounted at the shared rate, like every future benefit (the income gain's own wait is counted from delivery, in ln_income_gain_per_person).

rows.label: Counted less where the outcome isn't measured for this charity
rows.explainer: The shared missing-data step (docs/normalization.md 2.12): WVS counts its doses, but the effect on human deaths was measured only in Goa, by a pre-post model rather than a controlled comparison, and not where most of 2025's doses were given; so the branch is thin.

rows.label: All adjustments combined
rows.formula: evidence_adj * counterfactual_adj * attribution_share * implementation_adj * leverage_funging_adj * wait_discount * missing_data_adj
rows.explainer: The product of the adjustments above.

rows.label: Treatment costs averted, as a share of value
rows.explainer: 0: the Goa study saw no fall in post-exposure prophylaxis, the main treatment cost (it 'assumed that there was no reduction in PEP administration'); people bitten by any dog still get it.

rows.label: Rebound malaria from lost immunity, as a share of value lost
rows.explainer: 0: no immunity is lost by people; the shared malaria rebound doesn't apply.

rows.label: Investment of income increases, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: 0: no income gain to invest.

rows.label: Other effects: dogs and livestock spared rabies
rows.explainer: Dogs spared a rabid death (about a week of severe suffering) and livestock losses to rabies averted. Our judgment of their value against the human deaths, 1%, 0 to 5%: valued in healthy years at the site's animal weights, the dogs' days are worth well under 1% of the deaths. A side effect, weighed by the shared slider.

rows.label: Benefits and harms not modelled, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: Effects beyond the deaths, as a share of their value; a side effect, weighed by the shared slider.

rows.label: Deaths averted
Value of a death averted (units of value)
rows.explainer: GiveWell's moral weights for the age band of each death averted (under five, 5–14, 15–49, 50 and over), times your multiplier on the value of a life: the site's one value of a death (docs/normalization.md 2.7).

rows.label: Units of value from deaths averted
Units of value from stillbirths averted
rows.explainer: A stillbirth averted at the site's one value (@givewell_shared.uov_per_stillbirth, GiveWell's), times your multiplier on the value of a life.

rows.label: Units of value from later-life income
Units of value from illness averted
rows.explainer: A share of the deaths' and income's value, the base GiveWell's supplementary share has.

rows.label: Illness averted per person reached, in DALYs (before adjustments)
rows.explainer: 0: illness is counted once, in morbidity_value_ratio.

rows.label: Illness averted, in DALYs
Illness averted, in units of value
rows.explainer: The bridge from DALYs into units of value: the unit's conversion cancels it, so illness counts as healthy years whatever "Healthy year vs doubled-income year" is set to.

rows.label: Total units of value
rows.explainer: Illness and the other supplementary shares add to the modelled value side by side, as one sum of shares does in GiveWell's sheets; illness counted in DALYs comes in through its bridge.
